notes: Metadata refreshed for v1.15 (Gemini CLI route removed — Google discontinued @google/gemini-cli in favor of the Antigravity IDE). The pinned findings are UNCHANGED from the v1.12 capture: W012 fires on any external-CLI handoff and copilot/codex still trip it, so dropping one of three CLIs does not clear any finding. A verification run of `bash evals/security/scan.sh` on the v1.15 skill emitted zero findings for peer-review — no new IDs, no severity escalations — which is the scanner flapping (see below), not a cleared mitigation; the superset pin is deliberately retained. The pinned snyk-agent-scan==0.5.1 is non-deterministic for this skill: the package pins the client, not the scanner's server-side backend model, and across runs it has emitted W011+W012, then W007+W011, then W007+W011+W012, and (on v1.15) nothing at all. To keep the deterministic CI gate stable against this flapping, the baseline pins the SUPERSET of all observed findings — W007, W011, W012 — so any run that emits a subset reads as a cleared finding (an improvement, not a regression) rather than failing CI, while a genuinely new finding ID still trips the gate. All three are presence-based heuristics on features the skill needs: W011 (untrusted external command output ingested via `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`), W012 (external-CLI handoff to copilot/codex), W007 (insecure credential handling — the review templates quote a phrase anchor from the diff and the self/claude path can return unredacted diff content). Mitigations (untrusted-content boundary markers, stdin transport for the bulk prompt on codex, the Step 4b pre-flight secret scan that detects secret patterns and requires explicit confirmation before any external-CLI handoff, argument validation) are documented in skills/peer-review/SKILL.md `## Security model`. copilot remains the argv exception (documented there as a residual risk backstopped by the secret scan); codex keeps the untrusted bulk prompt on stdin via the `codex exec -` sentinel.
